newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian capital to invite bids for power projects.
newsitem.headline: Indian capital to invite bids for power projects.

text.p: State-run Delhi Vidyut Board (DVB) said on Friday it would invite bids for setting up seven projects of up to 100 megawatts each to meet a soaring electricity shortfall in India's capital city.
"The tender inviting bids from private power producers will be issued within a month," DVB chairman Naveen Chawla told a seminar of the Independent Power Producers Association of India (IPPAI).

He said the DVB planned to tackle the 1,000-megawatt shortfall in the capital's electricity supply by setting up a total of 12 short-gestation gas-based projects of up to 100 megawatts each. "Locations for each of the projects has been identified," he said.

India's capital is reeling from an acute power scarcity. The DVB has been forced to draw 1,100 megawatts from India's northern power grid since its own generation of 900 megawatts falls far short of Delhi's demand for 2,020 megawatts.
The DVB has been running large advertisements in local newspapers pleading with residents to cut back on their use of electricity.
"The use of air conditioners is herewith banned between 6.30 p.m. and 10 p.m.," one advertisement on Thursday said.

"Do not ask for temporary power connections for marriages, fairs or other functions," the advertisement added. "During the summer, do not use power for advertising and promotional activities like neon signs, decorative lighting, window displays. These are herewith banned even on generators."
Chawla said the DVB would neither provide counter-guarantees nor enter into power purchase agreements with producers for the 12 projects because of the "peculiar status" of the utility.

Although the DVB is under the administrative control of the Delhi state government, the federal government wields considerable influence because of the large arrears the utility owes to central utilities like Coal India Ltd and the National Thermal Power Corp.

Union Power Minister Y.K. Alagh told a delegation of IPPAI members on Thursday that his ministry's thrust will be to generate additional power through improvement in the plant load factor, an IPPAI official said.

The official said the power ministry had earmarked two billion rupees ($56 million) towards renovation and modernisation of existing plants and hoped to mobilise a total of 20 billion rupees through funds from financial institutions like India's Power Finance Corp and the World Bank.
The IPPAI is an association of 30 companies which produce 20,000 megawatts across the country.
-- Amitav Ranjan, New Delhi newsroom +91-11-3012024 ($1 = 35.65 rupees)
